summary: APM feed s066_single is degraded: 58.0% of TCP sessions (69/119) are one-way, exceeding 10% threshold and violating APM requirement for bidirectional traffic. All other checks (duplicates, drops, VLANs, encryption, overload) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding only one direction of flows to the tool - likely a single SPAN/TAP leg or RX/TX not aggregated, or asymmetric routing captured at a single point without pairing both sides.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM requires both request and response directions to correlate transactions and measure response time/latency. With 58% one-way sessions it will show incomplete transactions, missing response metrics, and inaccurate performance baselines.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregating both directions (RX+TX / client+server) at the packet broker ensures the APM receives complete bidirectional flows needed for transaction correlation.
